sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium was delayed by 45 minutes due to heavy traffic and large crowds. Inside, the audience was rowdy and boisterous. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In September 2016, NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick knelt during the US national anthem to protest racial injustice and police brutality. The action sparked widespread debate, inspiring other athletes while drawing criticism from political figures and leading to his exit from the NFL.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The protest became a defining moment for modern athlete activism and civil rights, influencing global sports movements like taking the knee. Kaepernick argues that sports and politics are inherently linked and that current societal conditions demand more prominent protest.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Ten years on, Kaepernick has published a memoir titled The Perilous Fight and continues his philanthropic work and community campaigns while maintaining his fitness in case an opportunity to return to the NFL arises.

gist: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. His career included loan spells at lower division clubs before breaking through at Tottenham Hotspur and later moving to Bayern Munich.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: He became the first English player to win the trophy since 2001 and the fifth overall, proving his doubters wrong through hard work and dedication.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: After celebrations, Kane returns to business with Bayern Munich playing Magdeburg and Borussia Dortmund, while targeting potential success with England at Euro 2028.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tottenham defeated Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, securing back-to-back league wins for the first time in 42 attempts. Goals and strong performances from players like Mathys Tel and James Maddison helped seal the victory, aided by a red card for Cole Palmer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The win moves Spurs up to 12th in the table and offers growing signs of recovery following a difficult period. Manager Roberto de Zerbi highlighted a recent honest team meeting as the turning point that changed the spirit of the group.

fivew: Tottenham secured a 2-0 away win against Chelsea.
